The paper studies the electromagnetic scattering problem from a perfect conductor.
The authors use the integral equation approach and boundary integral operators.
The solution to the scattering problem is represented by the combined magnetic and electric dipole distribution.
The operator Q combines the potential and the restriction operator.
The operator M is a boundary integral operator that represents the electromagnetic field.
The operator N is a boundary integral operator that represents the electromagnetic field and is shown to be infinitely differentiable.
Theorem 1 states that the operator A is Frechet differentiable and its derivative is given by the operator A(').
The kernel of the operator Q is infinitely differentiable in r.
The operators Tj and So are infinitely differentiable.
The mth derivatives of the operators Tj and So are given by the operators Tj(m) and S(m), respectively.
The Silver-Muller radiation condition is a condition that the scattered field must satisfy to be considered a solution to the electromagnetic scattering problem.
The operator P2 is a projection operator that projects a vector field onto the tangent plane of the boundary.
The operator Po is a projection operator that projects a vector field onto the normal vector of the boundary.
The operator fi is a boundary integral operator that represents the electromagnetic field and is shown to be infinitely differentiable.
The operator R(r)E' is infinitely differentiable.
The normal vector v(r) is infinitely differentiable.
The incident field E'' is analytic.
